extra.message: The `name` query parameter (line 19, default `config.SUPER_SECRET_NAME`, overridable via `?name=`) is interpolated unescaped into an f-string (line 38) which is then compiled and rendered as a Jinja2 `Template` (line 41) with no sandboxing (`jinja2.Template`, not `SandboxedEnvironment`). Since the user-controlled value becomes part of the template source itself rather than template context data, an attacker can inject Jinja2 syntax such as `?name={{7*6}}` (confirmed by the commented-out test at tests/test_main.py:39-42 expecting `42` to render) or full SSTI RCE gadgets like `{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}` to achieve arbitrary code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message:
The `name` query parameter is embedded directly into an HTML response string without any escaping (`f"

Hello, {name}!

..."`) and returned as `HTMLResponse` content (via the FastAPI `response_class=HTMLResponse` declared at line 18). Even independent of the SSTI issue on the same line, a request such as `?name=` is reflected verbatim into the page, resulting in reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: `SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN` is assigned a hardcoded literal value (`"5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n"`) directly in source rather than being loaded from an environment variable or secret store (the commented-out `os.getenv("SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN")` shows this was the intended approach). Hardcoded secrets are exposed to anyone with source access and cannot be rotated without a code change/redeploy.
